order.why: Contained 150 cm track; the 16000 end carries a hot tip plus a 2.2 cm MIP blob 5 cm away reading as a Michel (rule 3), so 16000 is the far end and the low-z, beam-forward end 16001 is the vertex.

A 227 cm track that is flat MIP end to end (61056 vs 56380 is noise, and p4 shows no Bragg at either end), so rule 1 says nothing and only rule 2 (lower z) picks the 11001 end; a tie-break stretched over 214 cm is barely evidence.

Rules 1 and 3: p4 shows a genuine monotone Bragg decaying from 155000 over the first 15 cm at the 19000 end, with two sub-cm Michel-like stubs sitting at that same end, so the cool 58399 end at z=8 is the start.

The upstream group (z 80-145) holds far more charge than the downstream EM fragments, and within it rule 1 is clean at 19002: the 39.5cm proton Braggs to 235k at 19000 and cools to its start at 19002. The rival hot stub cluster 65 is 42cm away and the proton does not point back at it.
Rule 1 V-apex: an 11cm proton 137k->208k starts here and the 82cm MIP track back-extrapolates onto it; 15001 is the same point 1.5cm away.

Rule 1/2: the 290 cm muon carries a 2.5 cm 195k e/cm proton stub at ~90 deg only at this low-z end (z=263 vs 477), the only nearby small clusters sit here, and the far end 14003/14000 is a single stopping end split by a fit break rather than a second Bragg.
Rule 1: the 8 cm proton rises monotonically away from here to its Bragg peak at 11001 while the 21 cm MIP muon leaves the other way across a 138 deg kink.

Hot-blob trap: the 62 cm track is flat MIP and only spikes in the final 1.5 cm, so that is vertex charge and not a Bragg rise; the 3.6 cm 128k proton stub leaves at 118 deg (a real prong, not a mis-split Bragg tail) and the debris cloud sits at this lower-z end.
The whole event is one 7 cm e stub that is hot at both ends and cool in the middle; 14001 wins only on marginally lower z and a marginally cooler end, so this is close to a coin flip.
Rule 1 at a degree-4 junction: the 28.6 cm segment rises away from 5002 to its hot stop at 5004, the other three prongs are flat, and the shower fragments trail downstream from 5002.

p4 shows 154 cm of flat MIP with no Bragg at either end, so the 1.33x rule-1 ratio carries no real signal and this is a near-tie; I break it with rule 2, taking the lower-z end 15001 (z=359) over 15000 (z=501).

p4 shows seg 15002 rising monotonically over its last 8 cm to 210k at 15001, tracking the stopping-muon template, so 15001 is the stop and rule 1 leaves 15002, which also carries a 2.4 cm stub and blob 61005 5 cm away.

Rule 1/5 combined: 17002 is the terminating end of the 451 cm forward muon and sits at the base of a diffuse EM fragment cloud (11 cm e prong plus 4.3 cm stub plus ~20 loose specks within 25 cm); no other candidate carries a long track, but rule 1 formally reads 0/3 so held below certain.

The far end carries a smooth 8-point Bragg tail (141k down to 80k over 4.3 cm at 9000) plus a 0.9 cm Michel-like blip 5.7 cm beyond, so by rule 3 that end is the stopping end and 9001 is the start; but a lone 276 cm track starting 15 cm below the top wall and going down at 46 deg reads just as well as a stopping cosmic.
Start of the 174 cm forward muon that exits at z=500; deg-3 with two short prongs, one of which (12117) rises away and stops, and it is the most upstream point of the active region.

Zoom shows a three-prong star at the lowest z with a 3.6 cm proton stub at 196820 e/cm plus two short hot branches, but rule 1 reads 0 of 3 away with one rising toward it and 15005 sits only 3.7 cm off, so I drop a tier.

Zoom shows a tight multi-prong knot where the 151 cm muon (rising away to 115187 at 9000) and a 2.1 cm proton stub meet; downgraded because the 68 cm proton attaches to 9007 only 2 cm away and I cannot separate the two junction points.

Rule 1 at the degree-4 hub 24003: the 24.6 cm proton rises 25k->290k away from it and the 21 cm electron prong 10k->220k, and the whole EM/hadronic spray fans out from this point; only the 3.3 cm split from 24002 that carries the long muon keeps this off certain.

The only structure is an 8.6 cm proton whose dQ/dx falls monotonically along the proton template from 270k at 3000 to 78k here, so this is its cool start end; a 2.2 cm MIP stub 2.3 cm away supports a vertex.
Rule 1 holds at both 15002 and 15006 (2.6 cm apart); I take 15002 because the 175 cm muon and the 16 cm proton (Bragg to 275k at 15001) both leave it, with Michel-like blobs at the muon stop 15000.
p4 shows two hot lumps with the dQ/dx minimum 3.4 cm from 9001 and 6.5 cm from 9000, so the point both halves cool toward sits nearer 9001, which is also the interior end of this 10 cm heavy blob.

Only junction in the event: the 65cm MIP track terminates here with no Bragg, and two short hot hadronic stubs (2.1cm at 77k, 8.3cm peaking at 96k) leave from the same point; the muon runs slightly backward in z, which costs a tier.
Sharp step at 17003 from 190k over the last 11 cm (proton stopping at 17001) down to ~80k MIP along the 310 cm muon that exits at z=500; prongs are 154 deg so not certain.
Event is one 167cm flat-MIP track with no Bragg; 25000 sits exactly on the z=501.0 downstream face so 25002 is the only interior end, but rule 1 weakly points the other way.

Rule 8: the event is empty apart from one 11.9cm sub-MIP blob at the anode whose profile humps in the middle and tapers at both ends, so there is no direction; 52012 taken only as the lower-z end (rule 2).

Rule 1: the 109 cm mu has a monotone Bragg rise into 16001, so 16000 is its cool end, and the hot 12 cm seg 59003 starts 2.9 cm away and Braggs at 59007 - 16000 is the junction both Bragg ends point away from (132 deg, not collinear).

Rule 1 at full strength - both segments rise away with genuine monotone Braggs, the 123 cm muon to 220k at 13000 and the 5.7 cm proton from 20k to 285k at 13001 - but the zoom and principal frame render the two prongs as essentially back-to-back (148.5 deg), so one tier down for the collinearity trap.

Zoom shows a clean ~90deg V at 18048: a 91cm flat-MIP muon leaves it for the x=-201 wall while a 50cm proton leaves the other way (18048->18004->18000, 17deg fit-break bend) and Braggs monotonically to 190k at 18000; the 300k at 18048 is a 2-point vertex blob on a flat 70-90k leg, not a Bragg.

Rule 1: the 88 cm proton-like track is 82k at 13002 and 206k at 13000, so 13002 is its upstream cool start and the lowest-z candidate of the whole structure; the competing deg-4 vertex 20016 is all-flat sub-11 cm segments sitting 19 cm off the track.

Topology plus rule 2: every dQ/dx reading in the event is flat, so 16001 is chosen as the only junction - the interior low-z end (z=236) of the 59 cm MIP track that leaves through the y=200 top wall at 16000, with a 3 cm stub attached.
277cm beam-aligned muon whose downstream end sits at the z=498 wall and therefore cannot Bragg, so the free upstream end 21001 is the start; several blips lie in the same z~247 plane around it.

Rule 1: four prongs converge at 13004 and its 3.7 cm neighbour 13005, including a 32 cm pion rising monotonically to a 140k Bragg at 13007 and a 59 cm MIP muon; p5 shows the rival low-z tangle in cluster 79 has transverse RMS of only 0.5-3 cm and far-near +0.1 to +1.2, so it is track-like and not a shower apex under rule 7.

The 257 cm track leaves the detector at z=499.9 (13000), so the contained upstream end 13002 is the start; it also carries a 365000 e/cm point and the small clusters 39009/40011 sit within 10 cm of it.

A vertex plainly sits in this 5-cm junction (a 15.9-cm prong with a hot 97060 tip and a 15.7-cm prong both rise away from 10003), but the 278-cm muon's first fit point is 10004, 4.7 cm away, so the id itself is near a coin flip.

Only real object is a 43cm MIP track whose 15000 end sits on the x=-201 anode face, so 15001 is the contained end; it is lower in z and the segment rises away from it, with debris blobs spraying downstream.
The 328 cm track changes y by only 6 cm over 310 cm of z, so it is beam-aligned rather than cosmic; 18001 is its interior upstream end while the downstream end branches and exits at z=500.

The two muon halves meet at 9002 at 177 deg -- one straight MIP track, so 9002 is a segmentation break whose 4 cm sub-MIP stub reads as a delta ray; the vertex is the muon's interior low-z terminus 9001, which carries a hot end point and a small companion cluster 6 cm away, while the far end exits at z=499.
Only structure is a 105cm beam-aligned flat MIP; 8000 sits on the z=500 wall so the mid-volume end 8001, with a small blob 7cm away, is the origin.
Whole event is one 5.3 cm proton; the p4 profile falls monotonically from 232k at 13000 to ~175k at 13001, so 13000 is the stopping end and the track starts at 13001.

Two independently fitted segments both read ~67k at the 17002 junction and rise monotonically outward to 202k and 235k, so the cool junction is not a fit artifact; tier dropped one step for the 167-degree back-to-back prong pair.
